newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mobutu moving to North Moroccan hotel- manager.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu moving to North Moroccan hotel- manager.

text.p: The ousted leader of Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko is expected to arrive on Wednesday in a north Morocco sea resort and stay there for up to six weeks.
"Mobutu and his entourage are expected to spend several weeks here...All hotel rooms have been requisitioned until August 20," a manager of Le Mirage hotel told Reuters.
Heavy security was seen around the hotel, and a police officer said: "One of his majesty's (King Hassan's) highest guests is expected to arrive here on Wednesday."
All access to the hotel was barred.
Eyewitnesses said police had been deployed between Tangier airport and the hotel.
Mobutu, who arrived in Morocco on May 23, had been staying at the 30-room Amphitrite hotel, next door to King Hassan's royal palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat.
When he arrived in Morocco on May 23, Mobutu was accompanied by a group of more than 30 people including his family, an official source said at the time.
Located on a cliff overlooking the Mediterranean Cap Spartel beach, Le Mirage has about 20 rooms and steps giving direct access to the sea.
Asked by Reuters about Mobutu's final destination such as Portugal, a Zairean member of Mobutu's entourage said: "I do not know whether Mobutu will leave for Portugal or elsewhere."
Earlier, diplomats said Mobutu might leave Morocco for Portugal after a short stay in France for medical treatment.
It was not known why Mobutu was moving from near Rabat.
Moroccan officials were not immediately available for comment.
